title: Issues board reads from one bd queue
description:
The issues board of `crabswarm preview` should feel live and cheap: a change made anywhere shows up on its own within the poll window, and a refresh or a navigation answers in about a second, however many tabs are open.

## Use cases

### 1. Edit a bead in a shell, watch the board follow

A user (or an agent) runs `bd update`, `bd close` or `bd comment` in a terminal while the board is open in a browser.

- Nothing needs to be clicked. Within the poll window the list re-sorts, the badge changes, the detail page re-renders.
- The delay is one poll window plus about a second. It is never "poll window plus twenty seconds".

### 2. Open or refresh the detail page

A user opens `/issues/{sourceId}/{issueId}` or reloads it.

- The header, rendered fields, comments, children and the dependency table all appear within about a second of the request.
- The dependency table shows every edge that touches the issue, both directions, exactly as today.

### 3. Many readers, one database

Several tabs, a reload storm, or the poll tick landing while a page loads.

- The daemon never runs two `bd` processes against the same beads database at the same time. Calls that would overlap queue and run one after another, in arrival order.
- Two identical requests in flight at once (the same listing, the same `bd show`) share one `bd` run and both get its result.
- A request that is cancelled while it waits in the queue (the tab navigated away, the daemon shutting down) leaves the queue; no orphan `bd` process is spawned for it.
- Different sources are different databases and stay independent of each other.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant B1 as Browser tab 1
    participant B2 as Browser tab 2
    participant D as preview daemon
    participant bd as bd (one at a time per source)
    B1->>D: ListIssues
    B2->>D: ListDependencies
    D->>bd: bd list --json (one run, shared)
    bd-->>D: listing incl. edges
    D-->>B1: issues + child counts
    D-->>B2: edges derived from the listing
    B1->>D: GetIssue
    D->>bd: bd show --json (queued behind the listing)
    bd-->>D: issue
    D-->>B1: rendered issue
```

### 4. Switch surfaces while issue requests are in flight

A user clicks Roots (or any other tab) while the board is still loading.

- The new surface renders promptly. Requests already in flight for the old surface do not hold the new one back.
- Static files the browser asks for on its own (`/favicon.ico`, assets) never wait behind API calls.

### 5. One vertical scroller

A user scrolls the board or a detail page.

- Exactly one box scrolls vertically: the content column. The page itself (the window) never grows a scrollbar of its own, at any viewport width, on the list, the labels page, the detail page and the Roots surface.
- The tab header stays put at the top; the sidebar stays put at the left.

## Usability requirements

- The browser's per-origin connection budget is respected: two long-lived event streams plus a handful of short API calls must fit under it without starving unrelated requests.
- No new configuration is needed for the common case. The default poll window stays as it is.
- Freshness: a request always reflects the database as of that request. The daemon does not answer from an older snapshot to look faster.
- Failure experience stays as today: a failing `bd` run turns into the same error on the affected RPC, and the poll degrades the live feed instead of taking the daemon down.
- A `bd` run started from a shell while the daemon reads can still collide with the daemon's run. That collision is bd's own behavior and is out of the daemon's hands; it should be rare because the daemon's runs are few and short.
design:
One `bd list` per source serves every read that today spawns its own process; the remaining `bd` runs are deduplicated and queued so the embedded dolt lock is never contended by the daemon itself.

## Goal

A board refresh or a detail-page load costs at most one `bd list` and one `bd show` per source, run one after another, and answers in about a second.

## Scope

- `crabswarm/issues`: `Client`, `Poller`, `Service`, `Summary`, `Edge`.
- Go fixtures under `crabswarm/issues/testdata/` and Playwright fixtures under `web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/`, re-recorded from the live database.

## Non-goals

- Changing the proto schema or the web client source. The RPCs keep their shapes.
- Making the poll interval configurable.
- Serving from a stale snapshot (stale-while-revalidate).
- bd's usage telemetry (turned off by the user, outside the repository).
- Running or managing a `dolt sql-server`.
- Lifting the browser's HTTP/1.1 connection cap in the daemon (h2c). TLS and HTTP/2 arrive with the reverse proxy the user is putting in front.

## Context

Measured on this repository's beads database, 62 issues, bd 1.2.2:

| bd command | wall time |
|---|---|
| `bd list --json` (all statuses) | 0.8s |
| `bd dep list` with all 62 ids | 18s |
| two concurrent `bd list` | 3.4s (serial would be 1.4s) |
| four staggered `bd list` | finish at 1.3s, 2.6s, 4.1s, 6.3s |
| ListDependencies RPC (whole source) | 21s to 23s |

Root causes:

1. `Service.ListDependencies` (`crabswarm/issues/service.go`) with no ids runs `bd list` to collect ids, then `bd dep list <every id>`. bd answers that with one query per id. The listing it already ran carries every edge: `bd list --json` reports a `dependencies` array per issue in the flat `issue_id` / `depends_on_id` / `type` shape, identical to `bd dep list`'s output (verified: 23 edges, same set).
2. Every read has its own `bd list`: `Service.ListIssues` runs two (filtered, then all-status for `childCounts`), `Service.GetIssue` runs one for the children, `Poller.poll` runs one every tick. Embedded dolt holds an exclusive journal lock per process; beads opens with `fail_on_journal_lock_timeout` and the driver retries the whole engine open under an exponential backoff (initial 500ms, multiplier 1.5, max 5s, no limit). Concurrent `bd` processes therefore serialize anyway, but pay the backoff sleep on every hop and are ordered unfairly.
3. The daemon speaks HTTP/1.1 only. Two of the browser's six per-origin connections are held by the event streams; the slow RPCs occupy the rest, and unrelated requests (`/favicon.ico`, the Roots surface) stall behind them. Making every RPC short is what fixes this in the daemon.

Files: `crabswarm/issues/client.go` (`Client.run`, `Client.List`, `Client.Dependencies`, `Client.Get`), `crabswarm/issues/poller.go` (`Poller.Run`, `Poller.poll`, `changedIDs`), `crabswarm/issues/service.go` (`Service.ListIssues`, `childCounts`, `GetIssue`, `ListDependencies`, `clientLocked`, `startPollerLocked`, `RemoveSource`), `crabswarm/issues/types.go` (`Summary`, `Edge`), `crabswarm/issues/fakebd_test.go` (the fake bd script), `web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/` and `web/e2e/issues.spec.ts`.

Fixtures: `crabswarm/issues/testdata/list.json` and `web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/list.json` have no `dependencies` arrays and key on `crabswarm-no2`, an issue that no longer exists. Both sets are re-recorded from the live database; tests and e2e expectations move to the recorded ids. Every recorded file states its producing command and bd version in a sibling `README.md`.

## Approach

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph RPCs
        LI[ListIssues]
        GI[GetIssue]
        LD[ListDependencies]
        T[poll tick]
    end
    R["Poller.Refresh (singleflight)"]
    LI --> R
    GI --> R
    LD --> R
    T --> R
    R --> D[diff vs baseline, emit IssuesChanged]
    R --> CR["Client.run: singleflight(args) over semaphore(1)"]
    GI --> CR
    CR --> BD[bd subprocess, one at a time per source]
```

- **Shared listing.** Each source gets its `Poller` when its `Client` is built, not when `Service.Run` starts, so RPCs work with or without the ticker. `Poller.Refresh` runs one all-status `bd list`, updates the diff baseline, emits IssuesChanged when primed and changed, and returns the summaries. `Run` calls `Refresh` on every tick. Concurrent `Refresh` calls collapse through a `singleflight.Group` inside the poller, so the diff and the emit happen once.
- **Derivation in Go.** `ListIssues` applies `ListFilter` to the shared listing: empty `Statuses` keeps everything but closed (bd's own default), `Labels` is all-of, `ParentID` matches `Summary.ParentID`, `SortByUpdated` orders by `UpdatedAt` descending with id as tiebreak, `Limit` caps. Child counts come from the same listing. `GetIssue` takes its children from the listing and keeps `bd show` for the text, comments and close reason. `ListDependencies` flattens `Summary.Dependencies` across the listing and, for an explicit id set, keeps only edges with both ends in the set. `Client.Dependencies` and `bd dep list` are removed.
- **Queue and dedupe.** `Client.run` keys a `singleflight.Group` on the joined argument list and, inside the flight, acquires a per-client `semaphore.Weighted` of weight 1 with the flight's context. Waiters that are cancelled return `ctx.Err()` without spawning anything. Flights run under `context.WithoutCancel` of the caller plus a fixed timeout, so a caller that disconnects does not abort a run other callers share.
- **Emit from RPC refreshes.** A refresh triggered by an RPC that sees a change emits IssuesChanged like a tick does. The browser then does one extra bounded refetch; the baseline and the event feed never disagree.

Rejected alternatives are recorded as `Decision:` comments on this epic.

## Public surface delta

No dependency change: `golang.org/x/sync` is already a direct requirement; `singleflight` and `semaphore` are subpackages of it. No proto change. No config, flag or route change.

```go
// crabswarm/issues/types.go

type Summary struct {
	// ... existing fields unchanged ...

	// Dependencies are the outgoing edges bd list reports for the issue:
	// what it depends on, whose child it is, what it was discovered from.
	Dependencies []Edge `json:"dependencies"`
}

// Edge gains the tags of the flat shape bd list --json prints.
type Edge struct {
	FromID string `json:"issue_id"`
	ToID   string `json:"depends_on_id"`
	Type   string `json:"type"`
}
```

```go
// crabswarm/issues/client.go

// removed:
// func (c *Client) Dependencies(ctx context.Context, ids []string) ([]Edge, error)
// type depRecord

// unchanged signatures; run now dedupes identical concurrent invocations and
// serializes all invocations of one Client:
func (c *Client) List(ctx context.Context, f ListFilter) ([]Summary, error)
func (c *Client) Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Issue, error)
```

```go
// crabswarm/issues/poller.go

// Refresh lists the source once, updates the change baseline, emits the
// changed ids when the baseline was primed, and returns the listing.
// Concurrent calls share one listing.
func (p *Poller) Refresh(ctx context.Context) ([]Summary, error)
```

```go
// crabswarm/issues/service.go

// issueReader shrinks to what the service still reads through a Client:
type issueReader interface {
	IssueLister
	Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Issue, error)
}
```

Fixtures (persistent test data, re-recorded from the live database with bd 1.2.2, provenance in a sibling `README.md`):

```text
crabswarm/issues/testdata/list.json            bd list --json --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed --limit 0
crabswarm/issues/testdata/list_changed.json    same, after one recorded edit
crabswarm/issues/testdata/dep_list.json        removed
crabswarm/issues/testdata/dep_list_single.json removed
crabswarm/issues/testdata/dep_not_found.json   removed
web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/list.json             same command as the Go list.json
web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/dep_list.json         removed
web/e2e/fixtures/bd-data/show_<id>.json        bd show --id=<id> --json --include-comments, per issue the spec opens
```

## Testing and verification

- Unit, against the fake bd (`fakebd_test.go`): N concurrent `List` calls record one invocation; a waiter cancelled while queued records none; the fake bd gains an env-gated exclusive-run check (`mkdir` lock, exit non-zero on overlap) so "never overlaps" is asserted, not assumed; `Poller.Refresh` emits once for concurrent callers and emits from an RPC-triggered refresh; `ListIssues` filters and sorts equal the previous bd-side results on the recorded fixtures; `ListDependencies` edges equal the recorded `bd list` arrays, filtered for an explicit set.
- Service: a detail-page-shaped burst (ListIssues, GetIssue, ListDependencies at once) records exactly one `list` and one `show`, and no `dep`.
- Playwright (`web/e2e/issues.spec.ts`): dependency table and list still render from the re-recorded fixtures.
- End to end: daemon with `CRABSWARM_LOG_LEVEL=debug` against this repository, browser detail page load and a tab switch; the log shows no `dep list`, non-overlapping bd timestamps, and the page answers in about a second.
- Repository grep for `dep list`, `Dependencies(` and `dep_list` after removal.

## Risks

- A listing-derived filter that differs from bd's own (label matching, default status set) changes what the board shows. Mitigation: the filter tests compare against the previously recorded bd-side results.
- `bd list --json` could stop reporting `dependencies` in a future bd. Mitigation: the fixture README records the version; the decode test fails loudly on an empty array where edges are expected.
- A detached, timed-out flight could keep a bd process alive after its callers left. Mitigation: the fixed timeout is short (tens of seconds) and logged.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With the daemon running against this repository's beads database at debug log level, loading a detail page records at most one `bd list` and one `bd show` for the source, no `bd dep list`, and no two bd runs of that source with overlapping start/end timestamps.
- [ ] The detail page and the board answer in about a second locally (ListIssues, GetIssue and ListDependencies each under 2s when fired together).
- [ ] Switching to Roots while issue requests are in flight renders promptly; devtools shows no multi-second Stalled time on `/favicon.ico`.
- [ ] ListDependencies for the whole source returns the same edge set as `bd dep list` over every id did (checked once against the live database and recorded in the plan notes).
- [ ] ListIssues honors status, label and parent filters and the updated-first sort exactly as the bd-side flags did, proven by tests over the re-recorded fixtures.
- [ ] Concurrent identical List calls collapse to one bd invocation; a caller cancelled while queued returns its context error at once; a flight whose every caller has left before it acquired the queue slot spawns no bd process (fake bd tests).
- [ ] An RPC-triggered refresh that sees a change emits IssuesChanged (test).
- [ ] `go test ./...` and the Playwright suite pass on the re-recorded fixtures; `grep -rn "dep list\|dep_list\|Dependencies("` over the repository finds no remnant outside history.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: shared-listing — one all-status bd list per source, owned by the per-source refresher, serves the poll diff, ListIssues (filters and sort applied in Go), child counts, GetIssue children and ListDependencies. Because every one of those reads is derivable from that listing and each extra bd process pays dolt's open-retry backoff. Rejected: per-invocation singleflight only (does not merge the differently-filtered listings). Delivered by: steps to be created after the gate.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: edges-from-listing — the whole-source ListDependencies derives its edges from the dependencies arrays of the shared listing and never runs bd dep list over every id. Because bd list --json already reports the same edge set (verified identical on this repository) and bd dep list costs one query per id, about 0.3s each. Rejected: caching bd dep list lazily (a second cache with its own staleness for a call that need not exist). Delivered by: steps after the gate.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: queue-and-dedupe — Client.run is wrapped in singleflight keyed by the argument list, over a per-client weight-1 semaphore acquired with the context; flights run under a detached context so a cancelled caller does not abort a run others share. Because embedded dolt allows one process per database anyway, so concurrency buys nothing and costs the backoff sleep and unfair ordering; the semaphore rather than sync.Mutex so a waiter can leave the queue on cancellation. Rejected: dolt sql-server mode (a server to manage for a read-mostly UI). Delivered by: steps after the gate.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: no-stale-while-revalidate — requests always run against the current database; the daemon never answers from an older snapshot. Because after the other changes a refresh costs about a second, and a stale answer would be followed by a second refetch when the poll emits the change. Rejected: serving the poller's last listing immediately. Non-goal.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: out-of-scope — bd usage telemetry (turned off by the user outside the repository) and a configurable poll interval are non-goals of this plan. Non-goal.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Discussion: explicit-ids — ListDependencies with a non-empty issue_ids list: keep Client.Dependencies (bd dep list) for that path, or derive from the shared listing too and delete Client.Dependencies, its testdata (dep_list*.json) and the fake bd dep branch. Options: (a) keep bd dep list for explicit ids; (b) derive and delete. Default: (b) — one code path, no subprocess, and the web client never sends ids.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Discussion: rpc-triggered-emit — when an RPC-triggered refresh sees a diff against the poll baseline, should it also emit IssuesChanged (frontend does one extra bounded refetch) or only update the baseline silently (the change is then announced by the next tick, up to one poll window later)? Default: emit, so the baseline and the event feed never disagree.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Discussion: fixture-strategy — Go and Playwright list fixtures lack dependencies arrays and key on crabswarm-no2, which no longer exists live. Options: (a) hand-add dependencies arrays in the recorded shape to the existing fixtures; (b) re-record everything from the live database and rewrite every test expectation. Default: (a).

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Discussion: connection-cap — the daemon speaks HTTP/1.1 only (no h2c); browsers allow 6 connections per origin, two are held by WatchEvents/WatchIssues, so long bd-bound RPCs starve favicon.ico and the Roots surface (observed 6-7s Stalled). Options: (a) rely on this plan making every RPC about a second, so the 4 remaining connections turn over fast; (b) additionally serve h2c (golang.org/x/net/http2/h2c) so one connection multiplexes everything and the cap stops mattering; (c) b as a separate handoff item. Default: (a) in this plan, (c) recorded as a deferred handoff item.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: explicit-ids — ListDependencies derives edges from the shared listing for both the whole-source and the explicit-id path; Client.Dependencies, depRecord, the dep_list*.json fixtures and the fake bd dep branch are deleted. Because bd list already carries the same edges, the web client never sends ids, and one code path beats a dormant subprocess path. Rejected: keeping bd dep list for explicit ids. Delivered by crabswarm-3hp.1, crabswarm-3hp.4, crabswarm-3hp.5.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: rpc-triggered-emit — a refresh triggered by an RPC that observes a diff emits IssuesChanged exactly like a tick. Because the baseline and the event feed must never disagree; the cost is one extra bounded refetch in the browser. Rejected: silently updating the baseline and letting the next tick announce it. Delivered by crabswarm-3hp.3.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: fixture-strategy — Go and Playwright bd fixtures are re-recorded from the live database (bd 1.2.2) with their producing commands noted in a sibling README.md; tests and e2e expectations move off crabswarm-no2, which no longer exists, onto recorded ids. Because the user prefers real recordings over hand-edited ones. Rejected: hand-adding dependencies arrays to the existing fixtures. Delivered by crabswarm-3hp.1, crabswarm-3hp.5.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: connection-cap — no h2c in the daemon and no handoff item for it. The user is putting traefik and authentik in front of the daemon for TLS, which brings HTTP/2 multiplexing at the proxy; in the daemon the fix is making every RPC short. Rejected: golang.org/x/net/http2/h2c in this plan; a deferred handoff item. Delivered by crabswarm-3hp.4 (short RPCs) and crabswarm-3hp.6 (measurement); the proxy is a non-goal here.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: shared-listing [amends: shared-listing] — same choice; delivered by crabswarm-3hp.3 (Poller.Refresh) and crabswarm-3hp.4 (service reads derive from it). Filter semantics in Go: empty Statuses keeps everything but closed, Labels all-of, ParentID exact, SortByUpdated descending with id tiebreak, Limit caps.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: queue-and-dedupe [amends: queue-and-dedupe] — same choice; delivered by crabswarm-3hp.2. Flights run under context.WithoutCancel of the caller plus a fixed timeout constant; waiters cancelled in the queue spawn nothing.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: edges-from-listing [amends: edges-from-listing] — same choice; delivered by crabswarm-3hp.1 (decode), crabswarm-3hp.4 (ListDependencies), crabswarm-3hp.5 (e2e fixtures).

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: single-scroller — the window never scrolls on the issues or roots surfaces; the content column is the only vertical scroller. The shell (Layout) owns the viewport with overflow hidden, and the element that escapes the scrollport today is found and fixed in a real browser rather than guessed. Because the outer scrollbar carries no value and the sandbox used for planning cannot run a browser to pin the culprit. Rejected: patching one suspected element without the shell change. Delivered by crabswarm-3hp.7; measured in crabswarm-3hp.6.

comments.author: ngicks
comments.text: Decision: flight-lifetime [automatic] — Client.run flights are refcounted: callers join through singleflight DoChan and select on their own context, so a cancelled caller returns ctx.Err() at once; the flight runs under a detached context with a fixed timeout that is cancelled when the last joined caller leaves, and the semaphore is acquired with that flight context, so a flight everyone abandoned before it reached the queue slot spawns no bd process. Because plain singleflight.Do under a detached context cannot both keep a shared run alive for the remaining callers and avoid a stray run when nobody is left. Rejected: detached flights that always run to completion (a stray bounded bd run after all callers leave); using the first caller's context (cancels the run for everyone). Acceptance criteria amended in the same turn. Delivered by the queue-and-dedupe step.
